core.text: A question can be asked straight (*Quid facit?* what is he doing?) or tucked inside another sentence — **an indirect question (a question folded into a sentence: nescio quid faciat = I don't know what he is doing)**. After a verb of asking, knowing or wondering (*rogat*, *scit*, *mīrātur*), the question word stays (*quis, quid, cūr, ubi, quōmodo, num*) but the verb goes into the subjunctive (the form Latin uses for wishes, purposes and what someone tells someone to do). Latin name: *interrogatio obliqua*.
English: *Where is he?* becomes *I don't know where he is*: only the word order changes. Latin changes the verb form instead.
Asking / knowing verb + question word + subjunctive: present after a present main verb, imperfect after a past one. 'Whether' is num or utrum … an.

invented.en: I did not know why the girl was crying.

core.text: *quis / quid* asks; *quī / quae / quod* (who, which) points back to a noun and keeps the indicative: *nesciō quid dīcat* (I don't know what he is saying — question) but *audiō id quod dīcit* (I hear what he says — a 'who / which' clause on a noun).

more.text: Also easy to confuse: a reported statement uses the accusative + infinitive (the 'says that …' pattern) — *dīcit eum venīre*, he says that he is coming; a reported question uses a question word + subjunctive — *rogat num veniat*, he asks whether he is coming. 'That' → infinitive; 'whether / who / why' → subjunctive.

The learner's notes: an indirect question is a question that forms a dependent clause inside another sentence; English marks it by word order, Latin by the subjunctive. Their examples: *sciunt ubi sīs* (they know where you are), *quaere ab eō quō eat* (ask him where he is going), *nesciō quid faciam*.

The question word can be *-ne* on the first word (*interrogāvī tuane esset pecūnia* — I asked whether the money was yours, Week 7), or *num* / *an* for 'whether'. For a question about something already over, the perfect subjunctive follows a present verb (*nesciō quis advēnerit*, Week 10) and the pluperfect a past one (*nesciēbam quis advēnisset*, Week 12). A deliberative question keeps its subjunctive when folded in: *nesciēbat quid faceret* — he did not know what to do. Ørberg's chapter 29 builds the pattern from *Quid faciam?* to *nesciō quid faciam*; chapter 32 adds *dubitat num … laudāverit*.
